params.text:
🌍 Climate Action Simulator

You are the Environmental Director of a mid-sized city. A major development proposal has arrived — a new factory that promises jobs but risks environmental damage.

Your decisions will shape the outcome. Choose wisely.

params.questionText: The factory will bring 2,000 jobs but emit significant CO₂. What do you do?

feedback.title: Economic Focus
feedback.text: You prioritize economic growth. The factory is approved without conditions.

feedback.title: Balanced Approach
feedback.text: You negotiate for cleaner technology. This takes more time but reduces emissions.

feedback.title: Environmental Priority
feedback.text: You reject the factory. The environment is protected, but jobs are lost.

params.text:
Negotiations Underway

You meet with the factory owners. They agree to invest in carbon capture technology but only if the city provides tax breaks. The community is divided:

  • ➕ Pro-business council supports the deal
  • ➖ Environmental groups want stricter targets

params.questionText: How do you proceed with the green technology deal?

alternatives.text: Accept the deal — tax breaks for carbon capture

feedback.title: Compromise
feedback.text: The deal is struck. Jobs are created and emissions are partially reduced.

alternatives.text: Push for stricter standards — no tax breaks

feedback.title: Strong Stance
feedback.text: You hold firm. The factory owners walk away, and the project collapses.

params.text:
Status Quo Outcome

The factory opens as planned. Jobs are created, but within three years the city's air quality drops by 15%. Public health costs rise, and citizens protest at city hall.

Lesson: Short-term economic gains can have long-term environmental costs.

Preservation Outcome

The factory is rejected. The environment remains pristine, but the city loses investment. Unemployment rises by 3%. Next election, a pro-business candidate wins on a platform of "jobs over trees."

Lesson: Environmental protection without economic alternatives can create political backlash.

Balanced Success!

The factory opens with carbon capture technology. Emissions are 60% lower than the original proposal. 1,800 jobs are created. The city becomes a model for sustainable development and attracts green investment.

Lesson: Compromise and innovation can deliver both economic and environmental wins.

Stalemate

Your firm stance leads the factory to relocate to a neighboring city with looser regulations. No jobs are created, and the factory still gets built — just somewhere else with fewer environmental protections.

Lesson: Uncompromising positions can lead to worse outcomes overall.

endScreens.endScreenSubtitle: Climate Action Simulator — Reflecting on your choices

l10n.startScreenSubtitle: Can you balance economic growth with environmental protection?
